Retain the base Arabic; the substantive later alteration is an explicit editorial emendation, not authority for replacing the early reading.

All seven English paragraphs faithfully preserve causal determination, the three alternatives for what is made, the four conclusions, and the two considerations of the effect's existence. No English change is required.

Retain the earlier attested wording and English, which intelligibly excludes every determinant rather than asserting self-production.

1428 p.7 regularizes «الصيرورة التي هو أمر نسبي» to «الصيرورة التي هي أمر نسبي». Record as grammatical regularization; early/base reading retained without changing the English sense.

Minor spacing, hamza, vocalization and paragraph division differences do not change the argument.

Later editorial commentary: All notes pp.5–8 were read: the neutrality gloss, extended justification and alternative formulation of the p.5 emendation continuing on p.6, references and competing causal definitions, classifications of what is made, and preferences to avoid describing an effect as a pre-existing recipient. The p.8 criticism of quiddity's derivative need explicitly treats بتبعه as possibly بالعرض. These philosophical criticisms remain attributed later commentary.

new.text:
Qum 1404 printed pp. 159–165 (canvases 163–169); 1428 edited digital text, vol. 2 pp. 13–25. Every stored Arabic and English paragraph, the complete early printed unit, and the later body and associated editorial notes were read. Printed witnesses only; no manuscript collation or independent human specialist certification is claimed.

Retain substantive early/base readings; repair four fused-word spacing errors and restore the omitted original printed Asfar reference as a separate source note.

All 51 English paragraphs were read against all 62 Arabic paragraphs. Necessity relative to another remains distinct from necessity through another; domain is not restricted to space; choice is not rendered as absence of causality. The difficult final act-will formulation is supported by both witnesses and remains faithfully literal with its existing note. The Asfar quotation follows the earlier Nihaya wording, with later divergences recorded. No English body change is warranted.

Later p.15 n.3 reports copies' «كانت هو» and removes هو; the present base already lacks it. Early p.159 visibly has the intrusive هو. This is an existing base/early variation, not a new adopted repair.

Later p.15 n.4 replaces early/base «معين» with «معا» on grammatical grounds. The early dual formation is retained; English 'together' already expresses the sense.

Later p.19 adds bracketed «إما» before واجب آخر and changes early/base «ليس معه» to «ليس معها» to agree with قطعة; record explanatory and grammatical regularizations without replacing the intelligible earlier text.

Later p.21 reads «الحجة على أن» where early/base have «الحجة أن»; syntactic expansion only.

In the Asfar quotation, early p.164/base read «بالاحتياج إلى الوجود» while later p.24 reads «بالاحتياج إلى الموجد». Retain the earlier quotation as transmitted by Nihaya; underlying Asfar has not been independently collated in this review.

Later p.25 n.1 replaces early/base «توقف الشيء على نفسه» with «تقدم الشيء على نفسه», expressly citing Asfar. Record the later editor's source-driven alteration while preserving the earlier Nihaya quotation.

Later p.25 n.6 prefers «الوجود المعلول» to early/base «وجود المعلول». Retain the earlier construction.

The compressed «كانت أحد الممكنات وراء العالم ونستنتج منها وجود أحد الممكنات» agrees with early163–164 and later23; no explanatory missing premise is invented.

Later editorial commentary: All notes pp.13–25 were read. They distinguish relative and conferred necessity; repeatedly criticize treating absences as causes; restrict cause to actual efficacy and distinguish capacity before action; quote Persian poetry on dependence; recast human agency as preparation; attribute the four determination theories to theologians; distinguish imaginary-time accounts; explain preference versus preponderance and the equal-path objection; discuss knowledge of benefits; and supply Asfar and Razi references. The editor's extensive disagreement with the causal account remains separate from Tabatabai's argument. The later claims about schools and underlying quoted works are attributed, not independently verified historical conclusions.

Original-note and boundary review: The entire early unit is preserved except the parenthetical Asfar bibliographic reference (ج٢ ص٢٠٣) after the quotation on p.165. Restore it separately, noting the later edition's expanded pp.203–204. No other early note or passage is missing.

All32 English paragraphs faithfully preserve the three limiting conditions, the complete/incomplete cause distinction, the quoted arguments, and exceptions for potential, successive and unordered infinities. Within the Shifa quotation, later pp.31–32 changes early/base «خاصية الواحدة» to «خاصية الواسطة», «خاصية» to «خاصيته», adds «مشتركا» before «في خاصية الواسطة», and reads «الجملة متعلق الوجود به، ومتعلق الوجود بالمعلول معلول» instead of early/base feminine «متعلقة... بها... ومتعلقة». Later p.32 adds «الآخر» after «كالواحد» in the Farabi proof and reads «فإذا» instead of early/base «فإذن». Retain earlier wording.

Base and later digital p.32 have «السلسة» in the concluding Farabi question; early p.169 has the normal «السلسلة». Repair this unambiguous dropped letter.

Later editorial commentary: Read every note pp.30–35: circularity gloss; cross-references; Shifa/Farabi source locations; catalogue of nineteen named anti-regress proofs; attribution of the ascent/descent distinction to Mir Damad and Sabzawari's extended commentary; the editor's objections to a chain of complete causes and to treating non-efficient causes as genuine causes; and qualifications concerning temporal succession. Qum 1404 printed pp. 180–186 (canvases 184–190); 1428 edited digital text, vol. 2 pp. 52–60. Every stored Arabic and English paragraph, the complete early printed unit, and the later body and associated editorial notes were read. Printed witnesses only; no manuscript collation or independent human specialist certification is claimed.

Retain substantive early readings, including terse and repetitive passages; repair five spacing defects and one misplaced shadda.

All36 English paragraphs compared with all50 Arabic paragraphs and both complete external units. The translations preserve first/second perfection, natural versus knowing causation, mental presence as a completing condition, higher reality/attenuated act, exigent versus actual satiety, and immutable self-perfection. The existing explanatory notes remain accurate; no English body change required.

Later p.54 n.2 explicitly inserts «اتحادا» into early/base «ويوجد بينهما تخيلا», printing «ويوجد بينهما اتحادا تخيلا». Retain the earlier attested terse wording. The English's 'imagined association' is an explained interpretation, not an assertion that اتحادا occurs in the earlier body.

Later p.56 n.4 changes early/base «حولها ويصدر عنها» to «حوله ويصدر عنه» by grammatical reference to كل نوع; it also reads «وإذا» for early/base «وإذ». Preserve the earlier formulation and idiomatic English.

Later p.57 n.4 deletes «ذاته التامة الفعلية التي هي» from the earlier repeated description, leaving «بغايته التي هي في الحقيقة ذاته التامة». Retain the early/base full wording and corresponding English; repetition alone does not prove an interpolation.

The other variants are punctuation, line/paragraph distribution and vocalization. No missing authorial argument was found.

Later editorial commentary: Every note pp.52–59 and final body60 read. Notes discuss Aristotle's motion definition, Avicenna references, end versus direction and a pupil's objection with Javadi Amuli's response, grammar of cognitive agency, explicit inserted اتحادا, substantial motion and Quranic allusion, objections to literal final causality, natural agency, grammatical changes, material limitation of acquired perfection, Sadra/Avicenna source attributions, and theological identifications. None is imported as an original signed authorial note.

Qum 1404 printed pp. 300–306 (canvases 304–310); 1428 edited digital text, vol. 2 pp. 265–273. Every stored Arabic and English paragraph, the complete early printed unit, and the later body and associated editorial notes were read. Printed witnesses only; no manuscript collation or independent human specialist certification is claimed.

The complete doctrinal text is retained. Five conservative spacing/spelling repairs are proposed, together with restoration of the original printed reference to al-Asfār VI, p. 370 as a separate source note. No paragraph of the original unit is missing.

All 23 English paragraphs were compared with all 31 stored Arabic paragraphs and the complete external unit. The translation preserves the two standpoints on divine proximity, the vertical causal qualification of human agency, and the distinction between necessity of a voluntary act and coercion. No English replacement is required. The phrase ‘acquire independence’ translates the early/base وتستقل and must be understood as dependent or relative independence through the Necessary, as the following sentence expressly qualifies it; the later editor's contrary wording is recorded rather than substituted.

Later p. 266 nn. 8–9 changes early/base به تتقوم هذه الروابط وتستقل to بها تتقوم هذه الروابط ولم تستقل. The first change regularizes pronoun gender; the second reverses the affirmative verb on doctrinal grounds. The note continuing on p. 267 itself admits that the inherited affirmative can mean the relations' relative independence with respect to their own effects. Retain the early/base wording and its translation, with this explicit qualification in the apparatus.

Later p. 269 uses الذي معه بقية أجزاء العلة التامة for early/base التي معه بقية أجزاء العلة التامة; later p. 272 has وهي أنه صادر where early/base reads وهو أنه صادر. These are grammatical regularizations, not grounds for altering the base doctrinal text.

Early p. 303 includes an inline reference (ج ٦ ص ٣٧٠) after the Ṣadrā quotation. The current base omits it; later p. 269 n. 5 identifies al-Asfār 6:370. Restore that bibliographical information in an attributed source note, without claiming independent collation of al-Asfār itself.

Joined digital tokens لااستقلال, إنّهوجود, فإنّهملا and الفاعلموجَباً are separated; السابقه is regularized to السابقة, confirmed by the early printed wording and later digital text. These do not change meaning.

Later editorial commentary: Read all associated notes on pp. 265–273, including the Ṣadrā introduction, internal chapter pointers, the two causal methods and their attributions, the non-spatial sense of encompassing, the long quotation from Ṭabāṭabāʾī's Asfār annotation distinguishing the proofs, Muʿtazilite and Ashʿarite bibliographies, competing scriptural arguments, the editor's stronger restriction of real efficient agency to God, and the identification of the middle position between delegation and compulsion. These historical attributions and philosophical objections remain later editorial commentary; their quoted source works were not independently verified in this collation.

Original-note and boundary review: Full early boundaries and all later notes were read. The omitted Asfār VI, p. 370 reference is proposed for restoration. No further original footnote or authorial passage is absent; later expanded notes are not silently imported as authorial text.

Qum 1404 printed pp. 306–307 (canvases 310–311); 1428 edited digital text, vol. 2 pp. 274–275. Every stored Arabic and English paragraph, the complete early printed unit, and the later body and associated editorial notes were read. Printed witnesses only; no manuscript collation or independent human specialist certification is claimed.

No substantive body variant, missing authorial passage, or correction requiring adoption was identified. The Arabic text is retained.

All four English paragraphs accurately preserve the distinction between life as an existential principle and knowledge/power as its consequences in animals, followed by the stronger claim of essential identity in the Necessary. The translation of مفارقة العلم الحياة makes the intended absence of knowledge from continuing life intelligible without reversing the relation. No English change is proposed.

Later editorial commentary: The long note on p. 274 was read in full. It quotes al-Qūshjī on competing definitions of life and al-Sabzawārī on life as existence versus life as apprehension and action, including their maximal divine senses. These quotations and attributions are identified as later editorial additions; their source works were not independently collated.

Original-note and boundary review: The early chapter contains no footnote or bibliographical reference missing from the base. Both boundaries and the later note continuation were checked; the full body is represented in Arabic and English.

new.text:
Qum 1404 printed pp. 307–308 (canvases 311–312); 1428 edited digital text, vol. 2 pp. 276–277. Every stored Arabic and English paragraph, the complete early printed unit, and the later body and associated editorial notes were read. Printed witnesses only; no manuscript collation or independent human specialist certification is claimed.

The complete body is retained. The later witness independently preserves the difficult wording already documented in the existing translation note; no unsupported emendation to knowledge is proposed.

All nine English paragraphs and the existing note were reviewed. Conventional designation, real signification, the higher presence of causal perfection, and comprehensiveness identical with detail are accurately distinguished. The objection's ‘set apart from power’ reproduces أفردا من القدرة in all three consulted witnesses. No English change is required; the existing qualification remains essential.

Early printed p. 308 and later vol. II p. 277 both read أفردا من القدرة in the final objection despite its immediately describing hearing and sight as aspects of knowledge. This confirms the base reading and the existing English note. The witnesses consulted do not support silently replacing القدرة with العلم.

Later p. 276 splits عدوهما as عدّو هما; this is a digital spacing defect and is not imported. No substantive body variant was identified.

Later editorial commentary: Read p. 276's Asfār citation concerning will/love, internal cross-references, and identification of the quoted analysis with al-Sabzawārī, including the complete versified passage attributed to Sharḥ al-Manẓūma p. 182. Read p. 277's Quranic and al-Kāfī illustrations of hearing/sight and speech as an attribute of act. These are attributed later notes, not original footnotes, and the source works were not independently collated.

Original-note and boundary review: No original early footnote or body passage is missing. Full beginning/end, quotation boundary, objection and reply are represented in both languages. The later verse and reference notes were read but are not promoted into the author's body.

new.text:
Qum 1404 printed pp. 308–310 (canvases 312–314); 1428 edited digital text, vol. 2 pp. 278–280. Every stored Arabic and English paragraph, the complete early printed unit, and the later body and associated editorial notes were read. Printed witnesses only; no manuscript collation or independent human specialist certification is claimed.

The complete body is retained, with two Arabic spelling/diacritic repairs. No substantive printed-witness variant or omitted passage was identified.

All nine English paragraphs were compared with all ten Arabic paragraphs and the external witnesses. The distinction between providence in deficient agents and in the Necessary, and the causal ordering of intellectual, imaginal and material realms, are accurately preserved. One clarification is proposed: the vague ‘everything possible that is established in it’ becomes ‘every contingent thing established in external reality’. This resolves the referent of فيه in the existing Arabic; the later editor expressly glosses it as في الخارج (p. 278 n. 2). It is a translation clarification, not an Arabic emendation.

The wording بكل شيء ممكن يستقر فيه is shared by the early print p. 309, base, and later p. 278. The later note explains فيه as في الخارج; no Arabic replacement is warranted.

Correct base دقةّ to دقّة and ثلاثه عوالم to ثلاثة عوالم, as confirmed by early p. 309 and later p. 279. These are typographical normalization only.

Later editorial commentary: All notes on pp. 278–280 were read: lexical glosses for يتوخاه and نقضي منها عجبا, the external referent of فيه, definitions of primary and secondary perfections, internal references to XI.3 and XII.19, and the Quranic parallels for beauty and precision of creation. These remain later explanatory notes and are distinguished from original body text.

Original-note and boundary review: No early original note, source reference, or paragraph is absent from the base. The chapter boundaries, three-realm enumeration and final conclusion are complete in both languages.

new.text:
Qum 1404 printed pp. 310–313 (canvases 314–317); 1428 edited digital text, vol. 2 pp. 281–286. Every stored Arabic and English paragraph, the complete early printed unit, and the later body and associated editorial notes were read. Printed witnesses only; no manuscript collation or independent human specialist certification is claimed.

The full unit is represented. Four conservative transcription/spacing/diacritic repairs are proposed. Later grammatical interventions are recorded without altering the inherited body. A difficult sentence about the soul and pain remains explicitly qualified in the apparatus.

All 17 English paragraphs were compared with all 20 Arabic paragraphs and both external witnesses. The translation preserves evil as privation, the distinction between an injurious existent and the privation itself, the attributed objection and reply concerning pain, and primary versus secondary intention. In the summary of pain, English construes كمال تلك القوة as the object of فقدها: the soul apprehends its loss of the faculty's perfection. This is a plausible contextual construal of the unvocalized early wording, but differs from the current base's nominative mark كمالُ and from the later editor's parenthetical punctuation. That interpretive choice is now disclosed; no silent substantive emendation is proposed.

Later p. 284 n. 4 explicitly changes early/base الذات التي يصيبه العدم to الذات التي يصيبها العدم. Retain the inherited body while recording the gender regularization.

Later p. 285 n. 1 changes early/base لعروض الأعدام to لعرض الأعدام. This is an editorial wording change; the original occurrence-language and its English rendering remain.

Early p. 312 and later p. 284 share the consonantal sequence تدرك النفس عنده فقدها كمال تلك القوة. The base marks كمالُ; later punctuation closes a parenthesis after فقدها and its n. 3 glosses the pronoun as the affliction. The current English instead understands the soul's loss of the faculty's perfection. Because the witnesses do not settle that syntactic difficulty, preserve the Arabic and explicitly identify the translation's construal rather than pretending agreement of all punctuation/vocalization.

Later p. 284 vocalizes وحدّه in منتزع من مرتبة الوجود وحدّه. The early print p. 312 and base have the same consonants; the English appropriately includes the limit of the existential degree.

Separate إيصالكلّ; join the accidentally divided كما لها as كمالها; repair بأصابة to بإصابة; and correct the first example's بشرَ to بشرّ. Early pp. 311–312 and later pp. 281–284 support the words; the last two are orthographic/diacritic normalization.

Later editorial commentary: All notes on pp. 282–286 were read, including attribution of the proof to Quṭb al-Dīn and Ṣadrā, three accounts of incidental evil and the long Mīr Dāmād quotation, attribution of the pain objection to al-Dawānī, and the complete quotation of Ṭabāṭabāʾī's Asfār annotation objecting to Ṣadrā's answer and proposing another distinction. The editor also records al-Sabzawārī's alternative, lexical/pronominal glosses, the mediated attribution of the fivefold division to Aristotle, and final bibliographical pointers. These disagreements are later contextual evidence; they are not used to rewrite the argument actually printed in Nihāyat. Underlying source works were not independently collated.

Original-note and boundary review: The early unit has no original footnote or bibliographical reference omitted from the base. The extended later commentary was read in full, including the note crossing pp. 282–283 and that crossing pp. 283–284. No missing original paragraph or terminal conclusion was found.
